outline.chapter_title: 1. Introduction to Reinforcement Learning for Language Models
outline.description: Sets the stage by explaining why RL is essential for scaling language models and highlights the stability challenges in existing algorithms.
subtopics: What is RL in language modeling?
Historical progress: from supervised learning to RL
Key success stories (Qwen, LLMs in math/programming)
Stability vs. scalability: why larger models need new algorithms

outline.description: Provides the foundational concepts and mathematical notation used throughout the textbook, ensuring students can follow subsequent derivations.
Deepens understanding of two pivotal RL algorithms that precede GSPO, illustrating their mechanisms, advantages, and shortcomings.
subtopics: PPO review: clipping, advantage estimation, value model dependence
Practical issues of PPO (memory, long sequences)
GRPO formulation: group sampling, token-level importance ratios
Illustrative examples of token-level weighting problems

outline.description: Examines the root causes of instability in large‑scale RL and motivates shifting from token‑level to sequence‑level objectives.
subtopics: Off‑policy learning in large batch RL
Why token‑level weights violate importance sampling
Accumulation of training noise in long sequences
Principle: unit of reward ≈ unit of optimization

outline.chapter_title: 5. Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) – Core Idea
outline.description: Describes the GSPO algorithm, its theoretical justification, and how it resolves the issues identified in GRPO.
subtopics: Clipping at the sequence level vs. token level
Choice of clipping ranges and their impact

outline.description: Derives gradients for GSPO and GRPO, comparing their weighting schemes, and explains why GSPO is more stable.
subtopics: Accumulation of unstable terms in GRPO

outline.chapter_title: 7. GSPO‑token: Token‑Level Variant for Fine‑Grained Control
outline.description: Introduces the token‑level variant of GSPO that allows per‑token advantage adjustment while preserving stability.
subtopics: Definition of sᵢ,ₜ(θ) and use of stop‑gradient
Relation to standard GSPO (numerical identity when advantages equal)
When to use GSPO vs. GSPO‑token

outline.chapter_title: 8. Experimental Evaluation – Training Curves and Benchmarks
outline.description: Walks through the experimental setup, hyperparameters, and key results demonstrating GSPO’s advantages.
subtopics: Training pipeline: batch partitioning, clipping settings
Impact of query set updates and longer generation length

outline.description: Explores the surprising observation that GSPO clips more tokens yet achieves higher efficiency, and interprets the findings.
subtopics: Empirical comparison of token clipping in GSPO vs. GRPO
Analysis of noise vs. signal in clipped samples
Why discarding more tokens can still be beneficial

outline.description: Explains the challenges of MoE training, the previous Routing Replay workaround, and how GSPO eliminates this need.
subtopics: MoE architecture and expert activation volatility
Problems with token‑level importance ratios in MoE
Routing Replay strategy and its overhead
GSPO’s sequence‑likelihood focus and immunity to routing shifts
Experimental evidence of stability without Routing Replay
Benefits: memory, communication, full model capacity

outline.description: Describes how GSPO’s tolerance to precision discrepancies reduces infrastructure complexity.
subtopics: Training vs. inference engine precision differences
Edge cases: partial rollout, multi‑turn RL
Impacts on distributed and federated training

outline.chapter_title: 12. Limitations, Future Work, and Open Questions
outline.description: Encourages critical thinking about the method’s scope and potential extensions.
subtopics: Choice of group size G and its effect
Extending GSPO beyond language models (e.g., vision)

outline.description: Recaps the key lessons learned from the paper and their significance for large‑scale RL research.
